decisions.reason: The source changes the LEDs' supply and data-drive design, but it does not change the indicator board's LED count, selected SK6812 model, package, part number, or color format.
Moving the LEDs to 3.3V does not revoke their separate standby power control, zero-current target, or GPIO5 control; the source provides no replacement switching topology.
A same-message MODIFY already removes the obsolete addressable_led_data_level_shifter_part BOM attribute, and the source does not change the selected LED component entry.
A same-message MODIFY already adds the addressable LEDs to the 3.3V measurement coverage; both rails remain measured and no other monitoring attribute changes.
A same-message MODIFY already removes the LEDs from the 5V powered-load list and narrows the rail to the sensor-power context while preserving the valid 5V sensor configuration.
The source changes only the addressable LEDs' supply and data logic; it does not alter any sensor-board connector, pinout, module interface, or sensor supply.
The standalone supply already powers the full shared 3.3V rail, so moving the LEDs onto that rail does not change the stated source-selection, regulator, activation, or load-coverage requirement.
The DCDC1 requirement still calls for a 3.4V configured output to maintain the system 3.3V rail; the newly attached LED load does not change that regulation target.
The source does not change any interboard connector type, pin count, pin order, or 3.3V/5V pinout.
The AXP2101 remains the normal source for the system and its DCDC1 remains the power-board-connected 3.3V source; the source does not alter the battery, USB, VMID, or VSYS power path.
The LED supply and data-level decision does not affect the ESP32 BOOT button, reset connection, or BOOT/EN capacitance.
Using the ESP32's 3.3V output directly for LED data does not change the selected ESP32-S3 module or its breakout requirement.
